To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Aβ induces oxidative damage via NADPH oxidases and PLA2, (2) Aβ induces NADPH oxidate and PLA2 in a ROS dependent manner, and (3) Aβ induces ROS production via NADPH Oxidease and PLA2.

the oxidative stress induced by Aβ in AD is mediated through the activation of NADPH Ox and its downstream signaling pathways leading to the activation of cytosol PLA2 (cPLA2) which in turn leads to the generation of arachidonic acid (AA).
Aβ increases ROS production in astrocytes and microglia via NADPH oxidases and that this increase in ROS activates PLA2, which leads to the production of neurotoxic lipid mediators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative stress in neurodegeneration, with a particular emphasis on Alzheimer’s disease.
elucidating the mechanisms of oxidative stress and inflammation in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease (reviewed by [1]).
the identification of the molecular targets of Aβ-induced neurotoxicity and oxidative stress in AD and the development of new therapeutic strategies for the prevention of AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NADPH oxidases are the major source of reactive oxygen in AD and that they are activated by Aβ.
NADPH oxidases and PLA2s play a significant role in the pathogenesis of AD.
the oxidative stress associated with AD is mediated by Aβ-induced activation of the NADPH oxidases and PLA2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NADPH oxidases are a key source of ROS in AD, and that NADPH-dependent ROS production is required for the toxic effects of Aβ.
NADPH oxidases and PLA2 are involved in Aβ-induced neurotoxicity and inflammation.
the NADPH oxidases and PLA2s are important targets for the development of novel therapeutics to treat AD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NADPH oxidases are a major source of ROS production in Alzheimer’s disease, and that targeting NADPH oxidates may be a viable strategy for preventing Alzheimer’s disease.
NADPH oxidases and PLA2 are key players in the neurodegeneratve processes in AD and targeting these pathways with natural antioxidants may be beneficial for the treatment and/or prevention of AD.
the neurotoxicity of Aβ peptides in AD is mediated in large part through the production of ROS by NADPH and the activation of PLA2s.
